_comment: How hard the fight is, chosen once per run beside the class.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS RATHER THAN A SETTINGS ROW. scenes/options.py is
drawn on the line that nothing on it may change how a fight resolves --
'a difficulty row would be a balance decision worn as a preference, and
the project's whole measurement culture rests on balance decisions being
made in data/ where they can be swept'. That refusal is still correct and
still stands. This is the other half of the same sentence: the decision
lives here, in content, with a sweep axis behind it.
ONE DIAL, AND WHY IT IS THIS ONE. 'incoming' is a per-mille multiplier on
damage arriving at the hero, and nothing else moves. Enemy health was the
obvious alternative and this project has already measured it as nearly
inert: the enrage threshold is a fraction, so a boss spends the same
PROPORTION of a shorter fight enraged, and both late bosses were
eventually tuned by damage after health changes moved the win rate by
nothing. A run with every permanent good maxed finishes with ONE point of
health more than a run that buys nothing, because past a point the hero
dies inside a stage rather than to attrition between them. Damage is the
axis this fight actually turns on; health is the one that reads like it
should and does not.
1000 IS THE IDENTITY, AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. At 1000 the multiply is
skipped by an early return and the arithmetic is the arithmetic that was
measured -- so 'Normal is the game the 280 cells were recorded against'
is a millisecond test rather than a twenty-minute sweep. Same trick as
attributes.py defaulting every field to the identity of its own
operation, and it is here for the same reason.
ROLLBACK: set every tier's 'incoming' to 1000. The code goes inert and
the game is arithmetically today's, exactly as loot.json switches off at
gold.base 0.
MEASURED: nothing below except 'normal', which is measured by every
recorded number in the project by construction. The other two are opening
bids and are marked as such until tools/balance.py --difficulty has swept
them. What must hold and is checked by the suite: the easiest tier still
loses every face-tank run. Only the ceiling and there is no game.
